name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q01 - Distillation and extraction purification techniques

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements regarding methods of purification of organic compounds:

Statement I: Simple distillation is suitable for separating liquids having a significant difference in their boiling points, such as chloroform (b.p. \(334\text{ K}\)) and aniline (b.p. \(457\text{ K}\)).

Statement II: In fractional distillation, each successive condensation and vaporisation unit provided by the fractionating column is called a theoretical plate.

Statement III: Distillation under reduced pressure is used to purify glycerol from spent-lye in the soap industry because glycerol decomposes at or below its normal boiling point.

Statement IV: Steam distillation is applicable to water-miscible organic liquids that possess a very high vapour pressure at room temperature.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Principles of Simple and Fractional Distillation
Simple distillation is used to separate volatile liquids from non-volatile impurities or to separate liquids having a large difference in boiling points. Chloroform (boiling point \(334\text{ K}\)) and aniline (boiling point \(457\text{ K}\)) differ by \(123\text{ K}\) in their boiling points and are cleanly separated by simple distillation. In fractional distillation, used when the boiling point difference is small, a fractionating column provides repeated cycles of condensation and revaporisation; each condensation-vaporisation cycle corresponds to one theoretical plate.

Step 2: Principles of Distillation Under Reduced Pressure
Distillation under reduced pressure (vacuum distillation) is employed for liquids with very high boiling points that decompose at or below their normal boiling points. Reducing the external pressure lowers the boiling temperature of the liquid. A classic technological application is the recovery of glycerol from spent-lye in the soap industry, where glycerol boils without decomposition under reduced pressure.

Step 3: Principles and Conditions of Steam Distillation
Steam distillation is applicable strictly to substances that are steam-volatile and completely immiscible (or virtually insoluble) in water. In steam distillation, the mixture boils when the sum of the vapour pressures of water and the organic liquid equals atmospheric pressure (\(p = p_1 + p_2\)), allowing the organic liquid to vaporise at a temperature lower than its normal boiling point. Applying this method to water-miscible liquids contradicts the foundational requirement of two immiscible phases.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The descriptions of simple distillation, the theoretical plate concept in fractional distillation, and the purification of glycerol under reduced pressure are chemically accurate, whereas the claim that steam distillation applies to water-miscible liquids is incorrect. Therefore, Statements I, II and III only are correct.

answer.text: Statements I, II and III only are correct
Statements I, II and IV only are correct
Statements II, III and IV only are correct
Statements I, II, III and IV are all correct

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q02 - Structure and stability of reactive intermediates

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements regarding reactive intermediates in organic reaction mechanisms:

Statement I: A carbocation has a sextet of valence electrons on the positively charged carbon, which is \(sp^2\) hybridised and adopts a trigonal planar geometry with an empty unhybridised \(p\) orbital perpendicular to the plane.

Statement II: The stability order of simple alkyl carbocations is \(\mathrm{CH}_3^+ < \mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}_2^+ < (\mathrm{CH}_3)_2\mathrm{CH}^+ < (\mathrm{CH}_3)_3\mathrm{C}^+\), governed jointly by inductive and hyperconjugation effects.

Statement III: An alkyl free radical possesses an unshared electron and is classified as an electron-rich nucleophilic intermediate.

Statement IV: A carbanion carries a negative charge on a carbon atom possessing eight valence electrons, typically exhibiting \(sp^3\) hybridisation with a distorted tetrahedral geometry.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Structural Characteristics of Carbocations
Heterolytic bond fission wherein the leaving group departs with the bonding pair of electrons generates a carbocation. The positively charged carbon atom possesses six valence electrons (a sextet). It uses three equivalent \(sp^2\) hybridised orbitals to form \(\sigma\)-bonds oriented in a trigonal planar geometry at bond angles of approximately \(120^\circ\). The remaining vacant \(2p\) orbital is oriented perpendicular to the molecular plane. Thus, this structural depiction is correct.

Step 2: Electronic Factors Stabilising Alkyl Carbocations
Alkyl groups attached directly to the positively charged carbon atom disperse the positive charge through electron-donating inductive effects (\(+I\)) and delocalisation of \(\sigma_{\mathrm{C-H}}\) electron density into the adjacent empty \(p\) orbital (hyperconjugation or no-bond resonance). With increasing number of \(\alpha\)-hydrogens and attached alkyl groups, hyperconjugative stabilisation increases: tert-butyl cation (\(9\text{ }\alpha\text{-H}\)) > isopropyl cation (\(6\text{ }\alpha\text{-H}\)) > ethyl cation (\(3\text{ }\alpha\text{-H}\)) > methyl cation (\(0\text{ }\alpha\text{-H}\)). Thus, the stated stability sequence is completely valid.

Step 3: Nature and Classification of Alkyl Free Radicals
Homolytic bond cleavage produces neutral alkyl free radicals containing an unpaired odd electron (a septet of valence electrons). Because the central carbon has seven valence electrons, it has an incomplete octet and is electron-deficient. Consequently, free radicals act as reactive, electron-seeking species rather than electron-rich nucleophiles (which must possess a donor lone pair of electrons). Characterising an alkyl radical as an electron-rich nucleophilic intermediate is incorrect.

Step 4: Structural Features of Carbanions
Heterolytic cleavage where carbon retains the bonding electron pair forms a carbanion. The central carbon carries a negative charge and an unshared electron pair, completing an octet of eight valence electrons. The carbanionic carbon is typically \(sp^3\) hybridised and adopts a pyramidal or distorted tetrahedral geometry with the lone pair occupying one of the hybrid orbitals. Thus, this description is correct.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The descriptions of carbocations, carbocation stability ordering, and carbanion geometry are scientifically accurate, whereas the classification of free radicals as electron-rich nucleophiles is incorrect. Therefore, Statements I, II and IV only are correct.

answer.text: Statements I, II and III only are correct
Statements I, II and IV only are correct
Statements II, III and IV only are correct
Statements I, II, III and IV are all correct
